description: Timing-accepted and physically validated 62.5 MHz instruction-refill profile, compared at identical clock and software with accepted 099154d.

diagnostic_and_model_evidence.description: Frozen model and root-cause evidence for completion-edge instruction responses and retained successful speculative RAM fills. No physical result is included.

linux_frontend_diagnostic.scope_caveat: First profiling-register access through process-exit marker, not only the timed CoreMark loop. Includes process startup, result formatting, kernel and background work. Twenty CoreMark iterations is not a reportable benchmark score.
linux_frontend_diagnostic.counter_caveat: No explicit canceled-transaction counter was instrumented. The cache-miss versus lower-grant difference is not an exact cancellation share. Hot conflict pairs show resident-tag collisions; they do not alone prove two-way-cache speedup.
linux_frontend_diagnostic.inference: The hot line is also fall-through beyond the index-search backward branch135b8->135a8, which retires57,740 times and redirects55,860 times. crc16 return155d0 retires only2,684 times. Repeated canceled fall-through requests can therefore preserve the same resident tag; resident-pair counts are not proof of equally frequent demand alternation. The public-port trace below directly reproduces the repeated-read mechanism.

repeated_canceled_fallthrough.scope: Public instruction-port trace equivalent to prefetch beyond a taken backward branch; no full CPU branch program. Warm dummy line aliases fallthrough by 0x2000; actual loop body uses another index.

coherence_audit.read_vs_posted_store: synapse_ddr3_system store_enq_req blocks enqueue whenever state==1 && !transaction_we_q, including the read-completion edge. New lower reads require !store_pending && !store_enq_fire. Thus no older posted write overlaps an instruction lower read/fill.
coherence_audit.following_store: Earliest following store snoop is the cycle after the lower-read completion; REGISTER_WRITES pending-fill metadata and byte forwarding include that fill and order the following snoop after it. The existing fill/snoop regression passes.
coherence_audit.unbuffered_writes: The physical fabric has a single active transaction, so no unbuffered physical RAM write can overlap the lower read.
coherence_audit.physical_address: ACCESS_WAIT bus_addr stays with the old granted physical read until completion; any same-edge restart captures its new address only at the edge, after old fill address/data have been sampled.
coherence_audit.permissions_and_TLB: Only final successful RAM ACCESS_WAIT reads fill. PTE_WAIT/TLB fill and all CPU response/fault stale gating are unchanged. A physical cache lookup always repeats permission checking through the normal translation path.

notes: Diagnostic 20-iteration Linux runs locate mechanisms and do not provide accepted CoreMark scores. Model 50+50 scores describe the specified AXI20 model; physical results below come from the real board.
All physical comparisons use the same 62.5 MHz clock, 25 Hz kernel tick, exact Linux image and application binaries. Bare-metal measured retired counts are identical for matched 1,686-iteration runs.
Linux profiler counters cover the whole CPU including kernel/background activity; events overlap and are not an additive CPI decomposition.

Compression uses a deterministic synthetic corpus, SQLite uses an in-memory database, and mixed-query statement counts have heterogeneous cost. Mesh compute medians exclude UART transfer; received FPS includes it.
The normal route failed setup. Only the bounded postopt implementation passed all required timing/CDC/skew/MIG checks and was programmed; existing warning/advisory entries remain.

comparison.scope: First profiling-register access through process-exit marker, not only the timed CoreMark loop. Includes process startup, result formatting, kernel and background work. Twenty CoreMark iterations is not a reportable benchmark score.

caveats: Twenty iterations and command-inclusive scope are diagnostic only; no accepted CoreMark score is reported.
Single matched run; privilege/kernel paths and physical page allocation can vary with changed timing.
Resident-tag conflict pairs are not validity-filtered in the unchanged harness; use the repeated hot pair and VA trace as evidence, not cold arbitrary tags.
No explicit canceled-transaction event was added, so miss-minus-grant is not a cancellation count.
The unchanged harness persists only the top128 entries per map. An absent named line/pair is bounded by the smallest retained count, not asserted to be zero.

matched_linux_frontend_diagnostic.scope_caveat: Twenty iterations is not an accepted CoreMark score. This is the whole command, including process setup, result formatting, kernel and background work. Retired instructions differ by +0.1367%, so the cycle change is not a pure identical-instruction IPC comparison.
matched_linux_frontend_diagnostic.top_map_caveat: Only the top 128 entries are retained. VA 0x135c0 is absent in the candidate with an upper bound of 170 misses; the dominant resident/requested pair is absent with an upper bound of 105 events. Neither absence proves zero.
matched_linux_frontend_diagnostic.crc_note: Both runs report identical CoreMark CRC fields and successful process completion; their short-duration warning remains diagnostic only.
